scope: Only the 26 named stranded members were judged. The two outer archive convictions were retained without re-judgment.
method: All 26 members: atomscan --no-update --follow=none --mode slow --format json, cleave facts, direct source/control-flow or ZIP structure inspection, and a final atomscan using this worktree via CLEAVE_TRAITS_DIR. Decoded facts were checked: no encoded executable layer was needed to explain these payloads. Incidental Base64 decodes of password-hash text were not treated as obfuscation. No payload was executed or connected to a peer. ZIP DEFLATE probes had a one-MiB output cap.
path_reconstruction: The Debian extractor had flattened data/usr/... to usr/... . The seven requested members were copied byte-for-byte back under extract/c3f630/data/usr/... before analysis and marking. Every copied SHA-256 equals the supplied member digest.

taxonomy_changes.stream_relays: Move both PHP read/write matchers from process/fd/stdio to process/io/stream, retain scope and matcher, and name exactly the indexed stream shapes rather than claiming proven child-pipe provenance. Update the only two exact YAML consumers. No ancestor directory selectors cover either moved leaf.
taxonomy_changes.root_shell: Add the structural unguarded-root-shell-main capability. Both existing hostile root-shell composites now require that body shape and root UID, preventing conviction on GID-only, guarded, or unrelated same-file calls. Generic root-ID/shell co-occurrence remains notable.
taxonomy_changes.coverage: Each member retains at least two hostile findings; no extra hostility was added to fill a count.
taxonomy_changes.controls: Ten focused fixtures are registered in testdata/expectations.toml. Four root-shell positives, four root-shell near misses, a stream-copy positive, and a different-value stream near miss passed focused analysis.

members.marker_note: Laudanum PHP command shell: no change
members.behavior: The allowed client IP gate precedes session login. POST username/password and nonce are checked against configured SHA-1 password hashes. Once authenticated, POST command becomes $command, cd updates session cwd, and other commands reach proc_open($command). Both child output streams are HTML-escaped into the session terminal output. This is an injectable operator-command payload; the access gates do not remove that function.

members.marker_note: Laudanum WordPress command shell: no change
members.behavior: Includes ipcheck.php for the client IP gate. Its command branch is explicitly if(true), bypassing the copied session-login branch. POST command reaches proc_open($command), and stdout/stderr are returned in the terminal form. Inspected sibling ipcheck.php checks REMOTE_ADDR against the three configured addresses and otherwise exits with 404; it has no process execution.

Before request dispatch, system() attempts chmod ugo-w and chattr +i on the file identified by __FILE__. The cmd request value reaches executeCommand(), which tries ReflectionFunction(system)->invoke(), call_user_func_array(), call_user_func(), passthru(), or system(). The intended reverse branch opens a socket and executes /bin/sh -i with FD 3 redirection, but uses undefined $ip/$port as request keys and assumes the socket is FD 3; it is not a reliable configured reverse connection as shipped. Permission and immutability changes depend on the executing account. The command-dispatch branch itself is an unauthenticated backdoor.

members.marker_note: Laudanum ASP command shell: no change
members.behavior: REMOTE_ADDR must equal the configured allowed IP or execution exits with 404. On form submission Request.Form("cmd") becomes cmd, WScript.Shell.Exec(cmd) starts the requested process, and StdOut.ReadAll() is written back to the response. A request can supply cmd.exe /c for shell syntax. This is an operator-command webshell payload, not automatic beaconing or an outbound connection.

members.marker_note: Laudanum JSP command WAR: no change
members.behavior: ZIP/WAR has five entries. WEB-INF/web.xml names /cmd.jsp as the Command servlet JSP. cmd.jsp accepts GET cmd and directly passes request.getParameter("cmd") to Runtime.getRuntime().exec(). It reads the child output through DataInputStream and emits each line to the HTTP response. No authentication is present. Runtime.exec(String) starts a process; shell metacharacters require a caller-supplied shell command.

members.marker_note: Overlapping ZIP expansion bomb: no change
members.behavior: Python parsed all 190023 central-directory entries: 4507981427706459 bytes declared expanded output from 45876952 bytes on disk. Local-header and stream extents overlap: for example first data offset 51, next 107, while the first compressed stream is 34144733 bytes long. Bounded raw-DEFLATE probes verified embedded later ZIP headers in early streams and a megabyte of repeated a bytes from the last stream, without expanding the bomb. This is a nonrecursive overlapping-stream resource-exhaustion payload. Cleave caps expanded member observations at 65536 and reports only 1554952742338126 expanded bytes in that partial population; those metrics undercount the full central directory.

main unconditionally calls setresuid(0,0,0), then system("/bin/sh"). There is no authorization or error check. This is a root-shell payload stub; the identity changes require existing root authority, capabilities, or a privileged installation. There is no kernel exploit or standalone route from an ordinary user to root.

main unconditionally calls setuid(0), setgid(0), then system("/bin/sh"). A comment describes compiling it and setting u+s, but the program does not install its own setuid bit. There is no authorization or error check. This is a root-shell payload stub; the identity changes require existing root authority, capabilities, or a privileged installation. There is no kernel exploit or standalone route from an ordinary user to root.

main unconditionally calls setuid(0), then execl("/bin/bash", "bash", NULL). There is no authorization or error check. This is a root-shell payload stub; the identity changes require existing root authority, capabilities, or a privileged installation. There is no kernel exploit or standalone route from an ordinary user to root.

members.marker_note: PHP reverse shell: relocate stream-copy traits
members.behavior: At load time the script optionally forks and calls posix_setsid(), changes directory to /, sets umask(0), connects using fsockopen(), and proc_open() launches uname -a; w; id; /bin/sh -i. Nonblocking stream_select() dispatches peer reads into child stdin and child stdout/stderr back to the socket. The same $input value is copied in each relay. This is an outbound interactive shell, not a listener. The configured private address is a destination, not evidence of a contacted C2 server. This WordPress template takes ip and port from POST, defaulting to 10.2.2.1:8888; unlike the WordPress command-shell template it does not include ipcheck.php.

@extract($_REQUEST) imports attacker-selected names into local variables. @die($ctime($atime)) immediately invokes the requested PHP callable with the requested argument and sends its return value to die(); callables such as system execute a command and can emit output directly. There is no IP or credential gate. This is variable-function dispatch, not Base64, encryption, PHP eval(), or sophisticated encoded obfuscation.
